why: A format name is only an identity if the declaration behind it is pinned to that name. The frames a verdict is derived from are read under the format the record names, so the declaration has to be the one that was in force when the record was written -- an edit in place would re-read every older record under columns it never had.

So each format carries its own copy of the declaration plus two digests. `columns_sha256` is over the live declaration in `ablation_harness.baseline_frames` (the columns, their kinds and units, the axis kinds, the required meta); `frozen_sha256` is over the stored copy itself. Editing either one turns rl_exp/tools/verify/test_baseline_contract.py red. The digests are written by an explicit paste (`--print-frames-frozen` prints them), never repinned automatically: a green run afterwards says the two agree, not that anyone approved the change. A column whose meaning, unit or shape moves therefore publishes a new format name, and the old one keeps its entry.

The ceiling, stated rather than implied: this table pins the *declaration*. What a frame is refused for -- a missing column, an undeclared one, axis labels that do not line up -- is behaviour, and it is pinned by the tests named in `cases` instead of by a second runner here. A case set in this file would be a copy of those tests, and a copy drifts.

yaw: base yaw, in the reward kernel's yaw-aligned frame
velocity_yaw: base velocity in the yaw-aligned gravity frame
command_world: command as issued this frame, world frame -- the x/y the reward kernel compares against the yaw-frame velocity, so acceptance reads the trained quantity
head_tail_force: sum of |net contact force| over the head/neck/tail bodies
tilt_cos: cosine of the base tilt, 1.0 = upright
non_foot_fraction: per-body normal contact force / body weight
mesh_min_z: lowest world z of those bodies' collision meshes (ground z = 0)
foot_contact: 1.0 where that foot carries more than 1 N this frame
foot_fraction: per-foot normal contact force / body weight
